'Provided' is the status of a feature, read through the lane's presence (observable_reading, status)."},{"span":"t12","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.alley","st.driveway_or_alley_entrance"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015, 'a highway: (1) Within a city block set apart for public use ... (2) Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'driveway' (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel') meets the highway at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance, 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'. tool_use_result.oldString: {"span":"t15","atoms":["ru.emergency_vehicle","ru.official_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"The performance of official duties is read through the vehicle that performs them (observable_reading, purpose), as the index maps 'in the course of his or her official duties; or' for NRS_484B_117_1: ru.emergency_vehicle, 'vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency', and ru.official_vehicle, 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment'. ru.emergency_vehicle is 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle': the words name official duties, not a response, so the class is what they read; ru.official_vehicle is 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle', which is why both are claimed."}
tool_use_result.newString: {"span":"t15","atoms":["ru.emergency_vehicle","ru.official_vehicle","sig.warning_lamp"],"derived":[],"justification":"Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): ru.emergency_vehicle ('vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency', 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle') and ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment') state what the vehicle is, never what it is doing; sig.warning_lamp ('a warning lamp lit') is shown by vehicles on duty and off it alike, and many official duties (a patrol, an inspection, a delivery of mail) show none. No conduct or feature the ontology carries tells a vehicle performing official duties from one that is not."}

{"node_id":"NRS_484B_270_3_o1","law_refs":["NRS-484B-270-3"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"t1","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"t2","text":"shall yield","role":"obligation"},{"id":"t3","text":"the right-of-way","role":"standard"},{"id":"t4","text":"to any person riding","role":"condition"},{"id":"t5","text":"a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter","role":"condition"},{"id":"t6","text":"or a pedestrian","role":"condition"},{"id":"t7","text":"as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]","role":"reference"},{"id":"t8","text":"on the pathway or lane.","role":"condition"},{"id":"t9","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t10","text":"shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t11","text":"within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t12","text":"except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t13","text":"(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t14","text":"(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t15","text":"(d) In the performance of official duties;","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t16","text":"(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t17","text":"or","role":"boilerplate"},{"id":"t18","text":"(f) In an emergency.","role":"sibling"}],"elements":[{"span":"t1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Motor vehicle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate' and is claimed with the admitted id, never expanded into classes, as the index maps 'The driver of a motor vehicle' for NRS_484B_270_1. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is no aggregate: ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency) and the atom reads the vehicle's class only."},{"span":"t2","atoms":["kin.speed","rel.contact"],"derived":[],"justification":"Reuses the index mapping of 'shall yield' (kin.speed, rel.contact). To yield is to give the other precedence: what the subject does is its motion, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity', read to tell a moving subject from one at rest; a failure that ends in a crash is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'. rel.contact is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss': the near miss is bounded by the operationalization of t3, not by this atom."},{"span":"t4","atoms":["kin.speed"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device; the ontology reads who controls a road user's motion through that motion, so the person riding is the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance, as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1 (observable_reading, agency). kin.speed carries no exclusion that applies."},{"span":"t5","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Bicycle', 'electric bicycle' and 'electric scooter' are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter); ru.aggregate is claimed with each admitted id, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter' for NRS_484B_270_2a_o1, and never replaced by ru.bicycle, ru.electric_bicycle or ru.electric_scooter."},{"span":"t6","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); claimed as ru.aggregate with that id, as the index maps 'A pedestrian' for NRS_484B_297_6_o1."},{"span":"t8","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"'the pathway or lane' is the pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters the line names: st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'. The other road user is on it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane to that road user so the rule reads its own lane l and not any lane of the scene; the obligation reads the same l again for the subject. Neither contract states an exclusion that applies."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"t3","standard":"the right-of-way: precedence owed where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)","concepts":["prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance"],"params":["p.conflict_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"convention":"traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[{"span":"t7","rule":"NRS_484B_297_6_o1","map":{"subject":"p"},"as":"condition"}],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle (ru.aggregate), read as driven through its controlled motion.","obligation":"For every road user p of the scene other than the subject, and every bicycle lane or path l (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) whose region p's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) at the observation, where p is either (i) a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, or (ii) a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian to whom NRS_484B_297_6_o1 applies (ruleApplies, its subject mapped to p): the subject's body is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject's footprint overlaps that same l while the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance and prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Read at every observation; an unobserved occupancy, contact or closest approach leaves the verdict unknown where it decides it.","params":["p.halt_speed_tolerance","p.conflict_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"t1","why":"'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observed, and the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"t4","why":"'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance: a rider halted in the lane is not read as riding.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"t2","why":"The yield is read on the lane the other occupies: the subject fails to yield where it touches the other, or where its footprint overlaps that lane while it moves with a conflicting closest approach to the other; a conflict while the subject stays outside that lane is not read as a failure to yield on the pathway or lane.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A car (member of the motor vehicle aggregate) turning right moves across a bicycle lane; its footprint overlaps the lane while a moving bicycle in that lane closes from behind, their closest approach falling within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The car halts short of the bicycle lane until the moving bicycle has gone by, then crosses the lane; while it overlaps the lane there is no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any rider in it."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"The subject is a bicycle (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) riding in the bicycle lane behind another bicycle."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The car's footprint is near the bicycle lane while a moving electric scooter closes on it with a conflicting closest approach; the source does not observe footprint occupancy, so whether the scooter is on the lane and whether the car overlaps it are unknown.","masked":["rel.occupies"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The car crosses the bicycle lane into a driveway; no bicycle, electric bicycle, electric scooter or pedestrian is in the scene."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A pedestrian walks in the bicycle lane while the sidewalk beside it is clear and unobstructed, so NRS_484B_297_6_o1 does not apply to it; the car enters the lane with a conflicting closest approach to the pedestrian but no contact."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"violated","narrative":"As branch_2, except that the pedestrian has stepped from the sidewalk into the bicycle lane to move around an obstruction on the sidewalk, so NRS_484B_297_6_o1 applies to it."}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.halt_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution","source":"speed resolution of the acquisition standard"},{"name":"p.conflict_horizon","unit":"s","value":3.0,"convention":"time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash","source":"traffic-conflict technique literature (time-to-collision thresholds)"},{"name":"p.conflict_centre_clearance","unit":"m","value":3.0,"convention":"centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width","source":"passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO)"}],"gaps":[],"gap_resolutions":[]}
{"node_id":"NRS_484B_270_3_o2","law_refs":["NRS-484B-270-3"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"t1","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t2","text":"shall yield","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t3","text":"the right-of-way","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t4","text":"to any person riding","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t5","text":"a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t6","text":"or a pedestrian","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t7","text":"as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t8","text":"on the pathway or lane.","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t9","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"t10","text":"shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive","role":"obligation"},{"id":"t11","text":"within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters","role":"condition"},{"id":"t12","text":"except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t13","text":"(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t14","text":"(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t15","text":"(d) In the performance of official duties;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t16","text":"(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t17","text":"or","role":"boilerplate"},{"id":"t18","text":"(f) In an emergency.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"t9","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is claimed with the admitted id. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, not membership (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'): it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency)."},{"span":"t10","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"Every verb is a way of having the vehicle's footprint in the lane: to enter is its footprint coming to overlap the lane, to drive within it is to overlap it while moving, and to stop, stand or park is to overlap it while halted. 'Stop' here is prohibited, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'); 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts too. Moving and halted together are every observation of the footprint in the lane, so the prohibition is read on rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', of a st.bicycle_lane_or_path region, whatever the motion; no exclusion of either contract applies. The exceptions of DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer') coincide with exceptions (c) and (e) and are carried there."},{"span":"t11","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane l to the subject. 'Provided' is the status of a feature, read through the lane's presence (observable_reading, status)."},{"span":"t12","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.alley","st.driveway_or_alley_entrance"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015, 'a highway: (1) Within a city block set apart for public use ... (2) Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'driveway' (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel') meets the highway at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance, 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'. That atom is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there', a distinction the exception does not need, since it covers alley and driveway alike. Entering or exiting is read through the subject's footprint (rel.occupies): its stretch in the lane l runs until its footprint overlaps such a region (entering), or has run since an observation at which it overlapped one (exiting)."},{"span":"t13","atoms":["sig.hazard","kin.engine_running"],"derived":[],"justification":"Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is 'both indicators flashing together', a signal, not the vehicle's condition; kin.engine_running is 'propulsion is available', 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt'. Neither denotes a disabled vehicle, and the condition of a road user is never an assumption."},{"span":"t14","atoms":["prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'). The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap the lane (rel.occupies rising), a member of traffic other than the subject was in conflict with it, prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. The primitives are 'Not a stand-in for: contact between bodies, the clearance between bodies, or the danger of a crash ... alone': they bound a traffic conflict under the conflict convention, which is what the words name, not a contact."},{"span":"t15","atoms":["ru.emergency_vehicle","ru.official_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"The performance of official duties is read through the vehicle that performs them (observable_reading, purpose), as the index maps 'in the course of his or her official duties; or' for NRS_484B_117_1: ru.emergency_vehicle, 'vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency', and ru.official_vehicle, 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment'. ru.emergency_vehicle is 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle': the words name official duties, not a response, so the class is what they read; ru.official_vehicle is 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle', which is why both are claimed."},{"span":"t16","atoms":["dev.human_direction","dev.governs","rel.occupies","st.travel_region"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180, 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') directing traffic is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}', with role police_officer; the direction reaches the subject where it governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region, the abstract union of the kinds dev.governs admits, among them the bicycle lane or path) whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), as the index maps 'or the directions of a police officer'. dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position': it is read as control of the region, not as where the subject must halt. The officer's authority is read through the direction's presence (observable_reading, status)."},{"span":"t18","atoms":["sig.hazard","ru.emergency_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is a signal, not a peril; ru.emergency_vehicle is a class and 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'. Neither denotes an emergency, which is never an assumption."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven, and its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a bicycle lane or path l (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) at the observation.","obligation":"At that observation one of the exceptions holds for the same l: (a) the subject's footprint overlaps l at every observation until one at which it overlaps an alley (st.alley) or a driveway or alley entrance (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance) (until), or has overlapped l at every observation since one at which it overlapped such a region (since); (b) [gap: a disabled vehicle]; (c) at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap l (the latest rise of its overlap, read with since), some road user u other than the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, had prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; (d) the subject is an ru.emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle; (e) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a travel region whose region the subject's footprint overlaps; (f) [gap: an emergency]. Where none holds, the duty is violated.","params":["p.conflict_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"t9","why":"'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"t11","why":"'provided' for bicycles is the lane's legal status, read through the presence of the mapped bicycle lane or path.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"t14","why":"The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains: a conflict with other traffic at the moment the subject came into the lane.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"t15","why":"'In the performance of official duties' is read through the vehicle's emergency or official class, the observable evidence of the duty it performs.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"t16","why":"The officer's authority is read through the presence of a person directing traffic in the police_officer role.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"t10","why":"Entering, stopping, standing, parking and driving within the lane are read together as any overlap of the subject's footprint with the lane, since together they cover every motion state.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A car drives along a bicycle lane for a block; its stretch in the lane neither begins at nor ends in an alley or driveway entrance, no traffic was in conflict with it when it came into the lane, it is neither an emergency nor an official vehicle, and no officer directs traffic there."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car crosses the bicycle lane; its footprint overlaps the lane at every observation until it overlaps a driveway entrance it turns into."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A car drives in the travel lane next to the bicycle lane; its footprint never overlaps the bicycle lane."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A car drives along the edge of a bicycle lane with no exception present; the source does not observe footprint occupancy, so whether the car is within the lane is unknown.","masked":["rel.occupies"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A police officer directing traffic governs the bicycle lane and the car drives within it at the officer's direction."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car swerves into the bicycle lane at an observation at which another car merging into its lane has a conflicting closest approach with it, and stays in the lane until it has passed."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A marked utility vehicle (ru.official_vehicle) stands in the bicycle lane."}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.conflict_horizon","unit":"s","value":3.0,"convention":"time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash","source":"traffic-conflict technique literature (time-to-collision thresholds)"},{"name":"p.conflict_centre_clearance","unit":"m","value":3.0,"convention":"centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width","source":"passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO)"}],"gaps":[{"span":"t13","kind":"atom","proposal":"ru.disabled | a vehicle that cannot move under its own power or cannot be driven on (a breakdown, crash damage, a flat tyre), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a halt, a set parking brake or lit hazard lamps — a vehicle at rest with its hazards lit may be fully operable | general","nearest":"sig.hazard (both indicators flashing together: a signal a driver chooses to emit, not the vehicle's condition); kin.engine_running (propulsion available; 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt', and a disabled vehicle may still run its engine). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may stand in or move through a bicycle lane, which the vehicle's condition, not its signals, decides."},{"span":"t18","kind":"atom","proposal":"env.emergency | a sudden peril at the observation that a road user's conduct answers to (a fire, a medical emergency, a crash or a hazard ahead), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** an emergency vehicle's class, its lamps or its siren | general","nearest":"sig.hazard (a signal, not a peril); ru.emergency_vehicle (a class; 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may enter or stand in a bicycle lane, which only the existence of the emergency decides."}],"gap_resolutions":[]}
{"node_id":"NRS_484B_270_4","law_refs":["NRS-484B-270-4"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"u1","text":"Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3 [NRS-484B-270-3],","role":"reference"},{"id":"u2","text":"the driver of a motor vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"u3","text":"shall not enter or proceed through an intersection","role":"obligation"},{"id":"u4","text":"while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"u2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"Reuses the index mapping of 'the driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_2a_o1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), since ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'."},{"span":"u3","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.intersection"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another'; '(3) The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', whose exclusion of the alley junction is the definition's own. It is 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line': the words name the intersection itself. 'Adjacent intersections' are two intersections with none between them along the way; the pedestrian is between them where its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) recorded as a directed approach to one of them, i1: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', the carrier being 'the stretch one direction of travel uses to reach one junction' — so nothing lies between c's stretch and i1 — and the other, i2 ≠ i1, is reached either through a second carrier the pedestrian also occupies that enters i2 (the opposing direction of a two-way way), or, where c is a lane (st.lane), through a lane that enters i2 and leads into c, directly or through one lane between (st.lane_connectivity, 'which lane a lane leads into'). The relation atoms tie both intersections to the pedestrian's own carriers; no distance stands for belonging. A pedestrian at either intersection is not between them: its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2, nor a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). st.lane_enters is 'Not a stand-in for: ... the region a device governs', which v3 reads separately."},{"span":"v3","atoms":["dev.governs","dev.traffic_signal","dev.stop_sign","dev.yield_sign","dev.inoperative","st.lane_enters"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') at an intersection 'in operation' is a device that controls that junction's traffic: dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head') whose state is not dark and which is not dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), or dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign. It is at the intersection where it governs it, dev.governs 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', or governs a carrier recorded as entering it (st.lane_enters), as the st.lane_enters contract directs: 'which intersection a device controls is read through both, or directly where the device governs the intersection'. dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position'. 'Official' is the device's legal status, read through its presence (observable_reading, status). lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_270_3_o2","law_refs":["NRS-484B-270-3"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"t1","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t2","text":"shall yield","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t3","text":"the right-of-way","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t4","text":"to any person riding","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t5","text":"a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t6","text":"or a pedestrian","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t7","text":"as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t8","text":"on the pathway or lane.","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t9","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"t10","text":"shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive","role":"obligation"},{"id":"t11","text":"within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters","role":"condition"},{"id":"t12","text":"except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t13","text":"(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t14","text":"(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t15","text":"(d) In the performance of official duties;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t16","text":"(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t17","text":"or","role":"boilerplate"},{"id":"t18","text":"(f) In an emergency.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"t9","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is claimed with the admitted id. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, not membership (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'): it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency)."},{"span":"t10","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"Every verb is a way of having the vehicle's footprint in the lane: to enter is its footprint coming to overlap the lane, to drive within it is to overlap it while moving, and to stop, stand or park is to overlap it while halted. 'Stop' here is prohibited, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'); 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts too. Moving and halted together are every observation of the footprint in the lane, so the prohibition is read on rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', of a st.bicycle_lane_or_path region, whatever the motion; no exclusion of either contract applies. The exceptions of DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer') coincide with exceptions (c) and (e) and are carried there."},{"span":"t11","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane l to the subject. (2) Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'driveway' (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel') meets the highway at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance, 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'. That atom is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there', a distinction the exception does not need, since it covers alley and driveway alike. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_270_3_o2","law_refs":["NRS-484B-270-3"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"t1","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t2","text":"shall yield","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t3","text":"the right-of-way","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t4","text":"to any person riding","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t5","text":"a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t6","text":"or a pedestrian","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t7","text":"as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t8","text":"on the pathway or lane.","role":"sibling"},{"id":"t9","text":"The driver of a motor vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"t10","text":"shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive","role":"obligation"},{"id":"t11","text":"within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters","role":"condition"},{"id":"t12","text":"except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t13","text":"(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t14","text":"(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t15","text":"(d) In the performance of official duties;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t16","text":"(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;","role":"exception"},{"id":"t17","text":"or","role":"boilerplate"},{"id":"t18","text":"(f) In an emergency.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"t9","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is claimed with the admitted id. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, not membership (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'): it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency)."},{"span":"t10","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"Every verb is a way of having the vehicle's footprint in the lane: to enter is its footprint coming to overlap the lane, to drive within it is to overlap it while moving, and to stop, stand or park is to overlap it while halted. 'Stop' here is prohibited, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'); 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts too. Moving and halted together are every observation of the footprint in the lane, so the prohibition is read on rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', of a st.bicycle_lane_or_path region, whatever the motion; no exclusion of either contract applies. The exceptions of DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer') coincide with exceptions (c) and (e) and are carried there."},{"span":"t11","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.bicycle_lane_or_path"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane l to the subject. 'Provided' is the status of a feature, read through the lane's presence (observable_reading, status)."},{"span":"t12","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.alley","st.driveway_or_alley_entrance"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015, 'a highway: (1) Within a city block set apart for public use ... (2) Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'driveway' (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel') meets the highway at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance, 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'. That atom is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there', a distinction the exception does not need, since it covers alley and driveway alike. Entering or exiting is read through the subject's footprint (rel.occupies): its stretch in the lane l runs until its footprint overlaps such a region (entering), or has run since an observation at which it overlapped one (exiting)."},{"span":"t13","atoms":["sig.hazard","kin.engine_running"],"derived":[],"justification":"Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is 'both indicators flashing together', a signal, not the vehicle's condition; kin.engine_running is 'propulsion is available', 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt'. Neither denotes a disabled vehicle, and the condition of a road user is never an assumption."},{"span":"t14","atoms":["prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'). The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap the lane (rel.occupies rising), a member of traffic other than the subject was in conflict with it, prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. The primitives are 'Not a stand-in for: contact between bodies, the clearance between bodies, or the danger of a crash ... alone': they bound a traffic conflict under the conflict convention, which is what the words name, not a contact."},{"span":"t15","atoms":["ru.emergency_vehicle","ru.official_vehicle","sig.warning_lamp"],"derived":[],"justification":"Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): ru.emergency_vehicle ('vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency', 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle') and ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment') state what the vehicle is, never what it is doing; sig.warning_lamp ('a warning lamp lit') is shown by vehicles on duty and off it alike, and many official duties (a patrol, an inspection, a delivery of mail) show none. No conduct or feature the ontology carries tells a vehicle performing official duties from one that is not."},{"span":"t16","atoms":["dev.human_direction","dev.governs","rel.occupies","st.travel_region"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180, 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') directing traffic is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}', with role police_officer; the direction reaches the subject where it governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region, the abstract union of the kinds dev.governs admits, among them the bicycle lane or path) whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), as the index maps 'or the directions of a police officer'. dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position': it is read as control of the region, not as where the subject must halt. The officer's authority is read through the direction's presence (observable_reading, status)."},{"span":"t18","atoms":["sig.hazard","ru.emergency_vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is a signal, not a peril; ru.emergency_vehicle is a class and 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'. {"node_id":"NRS_484B_287_1c","law_refs":["NRS-484B-287-1c"],"subject":{"binder":"subject","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"v1","text":"Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:","role":"reference"},{"id":"v2","text":"Between adjacent intersections","role":"condition"},{"id":"v3","text":"at which official traffic-control devices are in operation","role":"condition"},{"id":"v4","text":"pedestrians","role":"subject"},{"id":"v5","text":"shall not cross at any place","role":"obligation"},{"id":"v6","text":"except in a marked crosswalk.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"v2","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.travel_region","st.lane_enters","st.intersection","st.lane","st.lane_connectivity","st.crosswalk","st.entrance_of"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', alley junctions excluded as the definition's (3) excludes them. 'Adjacent intersections' are two intersections with none between them along the way; the pedestrian is between them where its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) recorded as a directed approach to one of them, i1: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', the carrier being 'the stretch one direction of travel uses to reach one junction' — so nothing lies between c's stretch and i1 — and the other, i2 ≠ i1, is reached either through a second carrier the pedestrian also occupies that enters i2 (the opposing direction of a two-way way), or, where c is a lane (st.lane), through a lane that enters i2 and leads into c, directly or through one lane between (st.lane_connectivity, 'which lane a lane leads into'). The relation atoms tie both intersections to the pedestrian's own carriers; no distance stands for belonging. A pedestrian at either intersection is not between them: its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2, nor a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). st.lane_enters is 'Not a stand-in for: ... the region a device governs', which v3 reads separately."},{"span":"v3","atoms":["dev.governs","dev.traffic_signal","dev.stop_sign","dev.yield_sign","dev.inoperative","st.lane_enters"],"derived":[],"justification":"'Official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') at an intersection 'in operation' is a device that controls that junction's traffic: dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head') whose state is not dark and which is not dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), or dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign. It is at the intersection where it governs it, dev.governs 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', or governs a carrier recorded as entering it (st.lane_enters), as the st.lane_enters contract directs: 'which intersection a device controls is read through both, or directly where the device governs the intersection'. dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position'. The law's words 'in operation' leave out markings and warning signs, which control no movement at the junction. 'Official' is the device's legal status, read through its presence (observable_reading, status). # Plan — batch 15 (iteration 1)

Eight laws, nine nodes. No law-local aggregates (`aggregates.jsonl` is empty). No new concept records: the nodes reuse `drv.interaction.overtake_pass`, `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier` and `drv.motion.complete_halt`, which earlier batches of this iteration proposed. The validator accepts every node. One node, `NRS_484B_270_3_o2`, carries three atom gaps and is not coded.

## NRS_484B_270_3_o1 — yield to riders and to 297(6) pedestrians on the bicycle lane

**Decision.** The subject is the motor-vehicle aggregate, with "driver" read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency). "shall yield" reuses the index mapping (`kin.speed`, `rel.contact`).

"the right-of-way" is the standard. Its definition, DEF-NRS-484A-210, sets the bound: "danger of a crash". It is operationalized with the closest-approach primitives under `p.conflict_horizon` and `p.conflict_centre_clearance`. It is not a surrogate.

**The other party.** It is quantified inside the obligation and has no binder. It is either:
- a moving member of the bicycle, electric-bicycle or electric-scooter aggregates ("riding", read as an agency reading, as the index maps "a person lawfully riding"), or
- a pedestrian for whom `NRS_484B_297_6_o1` applies. This uses a `condition` composition with its subject mapped to the quantified pedestrian.

**The lane.** "on the pathway or lane" refers to the "pathway or lane provided for bicycles…" that the next sentence names. The node carries it with its full qualification as `st.bicycle_lane_or_path`, anchored by `rel.occupies` to the other road user. The obligation reads the same lane again for the subject.

**What counts as failing to yield.** Contact, or the subject overlapping that lane while moving with a conflicting closest approach. This is disclosed as a narrowing on the obligation: a conflict while the subject stays outside the lane is not read.

**The composition.** It names only `_o1` of NRS-484B-297-6, because `_o1` is the node that carries 297(6)(c), the pedestrian's permission to use the bicycle lane.

**Branch scenarios.** `branch_2` and `branch_3` differ only in whether 297(6) applies to the pedestrian.

**Reversal signal.** If `NRS_484B_297_6_o1`'s applicability turns out not to cover a pedestrian already in the bicycle lane, compose `_o2` as well, or carry 297(6)(c) as a `definition` reference.

## NRS_484B_270_3_o2 — no entering, stopping, standing, parking or driving within the bicycle lane (blocked)

**Decision.**
- **The verbs.** Every verb is the footprint overlapping the lane, whether moving or halted. "Stop" is prohibited here, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope; the outcome does not depend on choosing between the two "stop" definitions.
- **(a) alley or driveway.** Read with `until`/`since` on the subject's stretch in the lane: the stretch ends in, or began from, an alley or a driveway/alley entrance.
- **(c) avoid conflict.** Read through conduct (purpose): when the subject came into the lane, a member of traffic had a conflicting closest approach with it.
- **(e) police officer.** Reuses the index mapping: `dev.human_direction` with role police_officer, governing the occupied region.

**Gaps.** Three exceptions have no carrier:
- **(b) disabled vehicle.** Re-filed as gap `ru.disabled` (pending G19 of smoke31).
- **(f) emergency.** Re-filed as gap `env.emergency` (pending G20).
- **(d) official duties.** The validator rejected reading this through the emergency or official class: a class is no evidence of what the vehicle is doing, and warning lamps show on duty and off it alike. It is filed as a new atom gap, `ru.on_official_duty`. The index maps the same words for `NRS_484B_117_1` to the classes; this node departs from that mapping for the validator's reason.

The node is not coded. Its law stays blocked until the gaps are decided.

**Reversal signal.** An ontology revision that adds a condition-of-vehicle atom, an emergency atom and an on-duty atom, or an operator ruling that the vehicle classes may carry (d).

## NRS_484B_270_4 — no entering an intersection while driving within the bicycle lane

**Decision.** The obligation is that the moving subject's footprint does not overlap both a bicycle lane or path and an intersection.

"Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3" is composed with `NRS_484B_270_3_o2` `as: compliance`. What subsection 3 "otherwise provides" is its exceptions (a)–(f). An `exception` composition would not work: it would remove the duty wherever o2 is engaged, which is every time the subject is in the lane. Compliance with o2 while the subject is in the lane is exactly "one of (a)–(f) holds".

**Consequence.** This node is valid but cannot be built until `NRS_484B_270_3_o2` is coded, so the law effectively waits on that node's gaps. The node does not inline the exceptions, which would only move the same gaps here.

**Reversal signal.** A ruling that "as otherwise provided" should be a `definition` reference borrowing the exception words.

## NRS_484B_270_5a — due care to avoid a collision with a rider (surrogate)

**Decision.** "Exercise due care" is a standard about state of mind, so the node is a surrogate.

While the subject moves, it must have no contact (from "to avoid a collision") and no conflicting closest approach (`p.conflict_horizon`, `p.conflict_centre_clearance`) with any riding member of the three aggregates. The catch-all character of "due care" is disclosed as a reading.

**Reversal signal.** Label evidence that riders at rest must be covered: drop the "riding = moving" reading.

## NRS_484B_270_7a — no intentional interference with a motor vehicle (surrogate)

**Decision.** The validator requires an obligation span, so the text is split:
- "shall not: Intentionally" is the standard (intent): a surrogate, operationalized through evasive braking and conflict.
- "interfere with the movement" is the obligation: the motor vehicle's motion (`kin.speed`, `kin.accel_longitudinal`), with the rider ahead of it (`rel.bearing`).

A violation is a moving motor vehicle, with the rider ahead of it, braking beyond `p.vehicle_evasive_decel` while their closest approach conflicts. `p.vehicle_evasive_decel` is a new parameter, proposed at about 0.4 g, above comfortable braking.

**Disclosed limit.** The node cannot tell intentional interference from accidental interference.

**Reversal signal.** Label disagreement on rider-ahead conflicts the car caused itself, for example a car overtaking too close. Such cases call for a condition on the rider's own deceleration.

## NRS_484B_270_7b — no overtaking a motor vehicle unless safe

**Decision.** The act is `drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, m)`, with occasion boundary `window` and window `p.overtake_window`. The node has no trigger, condition or exception spans, so the occasion maps no spans.

The "unless … safely" clause is a standard, not a surrogate. It is read in the obligation over the whole pass, from the concept's own beginning (the last observation with the vehicle ahead and headings aligned) to its recognition, using `since`. At every observation of the pass:
- there is no contact;
- the gap between bodies (`rel.surface_gap`) is at least `p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap`;
- no other road user has a conflicting closest approach with the subject.

The occupants are read through the passed vehicle's body. "can do so" is read through the pass actually made (perception). `p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap` is reused from `NRS_484B_270_2b_o2`, since it is the same clearance between a bicyclist's and a motor vehicle's bodies.

**Reversal signal.** The operator separates the passing-bicycle clearance into its own parameter.

## NRS_484B_280_1a — due care to avoid a collision with a pedestrian (surrogate)

**Decision.** Same construction as 270-5a, applied to the pedestrian aggregate.

**Reversal signal.** As for 270-5a.

## NRS_484B_280_1c — proper caution upon observing a pedestrian at the listed places (surrogate)

**Decision.** The validator requires an obligation span, so "shall: Exercise" is the obligation (`kin.speed`, `rel.contact`) and "proper caution" is the surrogate standard (closest approach).

**Trigger.** "upon observing" is `rel.visible`, a perception reading taken at the judged observation.

**Places.** "near" uses one new reach parameter, `p.pedestrian_near_reach`, for all the places:
- **(1) Highway, street or road.** Together these are every highway, so the node reads `st.highway`.
- **(2) Stops and boarding.**
  - "bus stop", "bench", "shelter" and "transit stop" are `st.transit_stop`. "stop" here is part of a place name, not the defined halt.
  - "boarding" is read through conduct (purpose): the pedestrian is within reach of a halted bus or transit bus with a door open.
- **(3) Zones and crosswalks.**
  - School zones and school crossing zones are "marked", so the zone sign is the atom (`dev.zone_sign` of kind school or school_crossing, through `dev.governs`). NRS 484B.363 is not in this corpus, so accordance with it is a status reading.
  - Crosswalks are `st.crosswalk`, marked or unmarked.

**Reversal signal.** Label evidence that pedestrians who were seen and are now occluded must be covered: read `rel.visible` in a window behind instead.

## NRS_484B_287_1c — pedestrians cross only in marked crosswalks between adjacent signalized intersections

**Decision.** The validator rejects narrowings on condition spans, so both conditions are carried as their words say, and the readings are argued in the justifications.

**"Between adjacent intersections".** It is read through relation atoms tied to the carriers the pedestrian occupies:
- **The first intersection (i1).** The pedestrian occupies a carrier that `st.lane_enters` an intersection i1. The carrier is the stretch from the previous junction, so no other intersection lies between.
- **The second intersection (i2).** It is found in one of two ways:
  - the pedestrian also occupies the opposing carrier, which enters i2; or
  - a lane that enters i2 leads into the occupied lane (`st.lane_connectivity`), directly or through one connector lane.
- **Exclusions.** A pedestrian inside either intersection, or in a crosswalk that `st.entrance_of` records as marking an occupied carrier's entrance, is at the intersection, not between.

**"Official traffic-control devices are in operation".** The words "in operation" limit the defined term (DEF-NRS-484A-145) to devices that operate. That means uncovered signal heads that are neither dark nor `dev.inoperative`. Signs and markings are posted or painted and do not operate, so stop-controlled intersections are not read.

**Crossing.** "Cross" is `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier` on the occupied carrier. The exception is occupancy of a crosswalk whose marked attribute is true.

**The reference.** `[LVMC-11-30-140-B]` names one law line with two nodes, so it is composed as an `exception` with both `LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1` and `_o2`.

**Reversal signal.**
- An operator ruling that stop and yield signs are "in operation". The fix would be to add `dev.stop_sign` and `dev.yield_sign` to v3.
- Label evidence on one-way mid-block crossings where lane connectivity is not mapped.

## For the operator

- **G19 and G20 (smoke31) still decide NRS-484B-270-3(b) and (f).** They are re-filed on the same words. A third atom gap, `ru.on_official_duty`, is filed for (d) "In the performance of official duties". The validator ruled that vehicle classes are no evidence of duty; that ruling also affects how the index maps the same words for `NRS_484B_117_1`, which reads them through the classes.
- **NRS-484B-270-4 waits on `NRS_484B_270_3_o2`.** It composes that node `as: compliance`, so it stays unbuildable until the three gaps above are decided.
- **The pedestrian and rider surrogates read conflicts by centre distance (270-5a, 280-1a, 280-1c, 7b's other-traffic check).** With `p.conflict_centre_clearance` at about 3 m, a vehicle passing close to a pedestrian standing at the curb can be flagged. The value is the operator's to review.
- **New parameters:**
  - `p.pedestrian_near_reach` (280-1c);
  - `p.vehicle_evasive_decel` (270-7a).

**Decision.** The subject is the motor-vehicle aggregate, with "driver" read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency). "shall yield" reuses the index mapping (`kin.speed`, `rel.contact`).

"the right-of-way" is the standard. Its definition, DEF-NRS-484A-210, sets the bound: "danger of a crash". It is operationalized with the closest-approach primitives under `p.conflict_horizon` and `p.conflict_centre_clearance`. It is not a surrogate.

**The other party.** It is quantified inside the obligation and has no binder. It is either:
- a moving member of the bicycle, electric-bicycle or electric-scooter aggregates ("riding", read as an agency reading, as the index maps "a person lawfully riding"), or
- a pedestrian for whom `NRS_484B_297_6_o1` applies. This uses a `condition` composition with its subject mapped to the quantified pedestrian.

**The lane.** "on the pathway or lane" refers to the "pathway or lane provided for bicycles…" that the next sentence names. The node carries it with its full qualification as `st.bicycle_lane_or_path`, anchored by `rel.occupies` to the other road user. The obligation reads the same lane again for the subject.

**What counts as failing to yield.** Contact, or the subject overlapping that lane while moving with a conflicting closest approach. This is disclosed as a narrowing on the obligation: a conflict while the subject stays outside the lane is not read.

**The composition.** It names only `_o1` of NRS-484B-297-6, because `_o1` is the node that carries 297(6)(c), the pedestrian's permission to use the bicycle lane.

**Branch scenarios.** `branch_2` and `branch_3` differ only in whether 297(6) applies to the pedestrian.

**Reversal signal.** If `NRS_484B_297_6_o1`'s applicability turns out not to cover a pedestrian already in the bicycle lane, compose `_o2` as well, or carry 297(6)(c) as a `definition` reference.

- **(c) avoid conflict.** Read through conduct (purpose): when the subject came into the lane, a member of traffic had a conflicting closest approach with it.
- **(e) police officer.** Reuses the index mapping: `dev.human_direction` with role police_officer, governing the occupied region.

**Gaps.** Three exceptions have no carrier:
- **(b) disabled vehicle.** Re-filed as gap `ru.disabled` (pending G19 of smoke31).
- **(f) emergency.** Re-filed as gap `env.emergency` (pending G20).
- **(d) official duties.** The validator rejected reading this through the emergency or official class: a class is no evidence of what the vehicle is doing, and warning lamps show on duty and off it alike. It is filed as a new atom gap, `ru.on_official_duty`. The index maps the same words for `NRS_484B_117_1` to the classes; this node departs from that mapping for the validator's reason.

The node is not coded. Its law stays blocked until the gaps are decided.

**Reversal signal.** An ontology revision that adds a condition-of-vehicle atom, an emergency atom and an on-duty atom, or an operator ruling that the vehicle classes may carry (d).

## NRS_484B_270_4 — no entering an intersection while driving within the bicycle lane

**Decision.** The obligation is that the moving subject's footprint does not overlap both a bicycle lane or path and an intersection.

"Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3" is composed with `NRS_484B_270_3_o2` `as: compliance`. What subsection 3 "otherwise provides" is its exceptions (a)–(f). An `exception` composition would not work: it would remove the duty wherever o2 is engaged, which is every time the subject is in the lane. Compliance with o2 while the subject is in the lane is exactly "one of (a)–(f) holds".

**Consequence.** This node is valid but cannot be built until `NRS_484B_270_3_o2` is coded, so the law effectively waits on that node's gaps. The node does not inline the exceptions, which would only move the same gaps here.

**Reversal signal.** A ruling that "as otherwise provided" should be a `definition` reference borrowing the exception words.

## NRS_484B_270_5a — due care to avoid a collision with a rider (surrogate)

**Decision.** "Exercise due care" is a standard about state of mind, so the node is a surrogate.

While the subject moves, it must have no contact (from "to avoid a collision") and no conflicting closest approach (`p.conflict_horizon`, `p.conflict_centre_clearance`) with any riding member of the three aggregates. The catch-all character of "due care" is disclosed as a reading.

**Reversal signal.** Label evidence that riders at rest must be covered: drop the "riding = moving" reading.

**Decision.** The validator requires an obligation span, so the text is split:

**Disclosed limit.** The node cannot tell intentional interference from accidental interference.

**Reversal signal.** Label disagreement on rider-ahead conflicts the car caused itself, for example a car overtaking too close. Such cases call for a condition on the rider's own deceleration.

**Decision.** The act is `drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, m)`, with occasion boundary `window` and window `p.overtake_window`. The node has no trigger, condition or exception spans, so the occasion maps no spans.

- there is no contact;
- the gap between bodies (`rel.surface_gap`) is at least `p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap`;
- no other road user has a conflicting closest approach with the subject.

**Reversal signal.** The operator separates the passing-bicycle clearance into its own parameter.

**Decision.** Same construction as 270-5a, applied to the pedestrian aggregate.

**Reversal signal.** As for 270-5a.

**Decision.** The validator requires an obligation span, so "shall: Exercise" is the obligation (`kin.speed`, `rel.contact`) and "proper caution" is the surrogate standard (closest approach).

  - "boarding" is read through conduct (purpose): the pedestrian is within reach of a halted bus or transit bus with a door open.

**Also waiting: NRS-484B-270-4** (don't drive through an intersection in a bicycle lane). - **NRS-484B-287-1c (no crossing outside a marked crosswalk):** I read "official traffic-control devices are in operation" as working signal heads only. Signs and markings don't "operate", so stop-sign intersections don't trigger the rule. If you rule that signs count, stop and yield signs get added to that condition.
- **"Between adjacent intersections" in the same law:** this is read from which intersection each road segment the pedestrian is on leads into. On a one-way road, the intersection behind is only found if the map records how the lanes connect.
- **Yield to cyclists and pedestrians (270-3 o1):** a failure to yield only counts when the car is inside the bicycle lane itself.
- **"Riding" (270-3 o1, 270-5a):** read as the bicycle or scooter moving, so a rider stopped in the lane isn't covered.
- **"Upon observing" (280-1c):** read as the pedestrian being visible at that moment, so a pedestrian seen earlier and now hidden isn't covered.
- **Pedestrians covered by the yield duty (270-3 o1):** the duty toward pedestrians composes only the first node of NRS-484B-297-6. That is the node carrying the permission to walk in the bicycle lane.

**New parameters for review.** `p.pedestrian_near_reach` (3.0 m) is the single distance used for every "near" in 280-1c. `p.vehicle_evasive_decel` (4.0 m/s², about 0.4 g) is the hard-braking threshold in 270-7a. Separately, the shared conflict clearance of about 3 m centre-to-centre may flag a car passing close to a pedestrian standing at the curb.
